# Hydrodynamics — Fluids

Unformalized claims gathered verbatim from [wiphy.org](https://wiphy.org/) (query: “relativistic hydrodynamics holography”).

claims.name: convergence_relativistic_hydrodynamics_charged_fluids
claims.statement: The convergence of relativistic hydrodynamics in charged fluids is investigated within the framework of holography.

sources.title: Quasinormal modes in charged fluids at complex momentum

claims.name: review_synthesizes_recent_progress_relativistic
claims.statement: This review synthesizes recent progress on relativistic hydrodynamic attractors, emphasizing applications to heavy ion collisions and the quark-gluon plasma. It frames the subject pedagogically through the effective descriptions most relevant in high-energy physics, namely hydrodynamics, holography, and kinetic theory, and highlights recent advances.

sources.title: Hydrodynamic attractors in heavy ion collisions: a review

claims.name: dissertation_introduces_causal_stable_formulations
claims.statement: This dissertation introduces causal and stable formulations of relativistic viscous hydrodynamics, establishing constraints on short-wavelength dispersion relations to guarantee stability in all reference frames. It extracts first-order causal theories from kinetic theory and holography, and develops causal models for charged plasmas and superfluids.

claims.name: review_uses_holography_especially_rotating
claims.statement: This review uses holography, especially rotating Myers-Perry black holes, to synthesize what is known about relativistic hydrodynamics under rotation: rotating strongly coupled fluids can behave like boosted fluids, like genuinely distinct hydrodynamic systems, or show no clear hydrodynamic regime at all. It also summarizes how hydrodynamic and non-hydrodynamic modes are extracted, how radii of convergence are computed, and what these results imply about the limits of hydrodynamics in rotating settings.

sources.title: Relativistic Hydrodynamics under Rotation: Prospects & Limitations from a Holographic Perspective
